chunks: "For each of these I'd start by asking about the edge cases and the language, then write it, then test it by hand.
Reverse a string: two indices, one at each end, swap and move inward until they meet.
In C I'd do it in place and make sure to handle the empty string, since computing length minus one on an unsigned zero is a classic bug. It's linear time, constant extra space.
Palindrome: same two pointers, comparing instead of swapping, and I'd ask whether to ignore case and punctuation. If yes, skip non-alphanumeric characters.
Substring search: for each starting offset in the haystack, compare the needle character by character. That's O(n times m) worst case.
I'd mention KMP gets it to O(n plus m), but for short strings the simple loop is fine, and in practice I'd call strstr or Python's in .
File parsing: open the file, read line by line so memory is constant, apply a regex or substring test, and write modified lines to a new file, then swap it in.
I'd handle a missing file and not edit in place.
For API design pseudocode, I'd define the handle, an init that returns an error code, read and close functions, and say who owns memory and what happens on timeouts.
For example a temperature sensor driver."
